seed: The starter Secondary button is the mock's glass (button.css .btn.secondary: --glass over backdrop-filter blur 12): over a busy screenshot, the text behind it is softened to a wash so its own words read, where it used to show through sharp at a quarter strength. Drops a Button on a screenshot full of small coloured code, at Next defaults, picks Secondary and photographs it up close. Then draws a rectangle, fades it, adds a Blur from the Effects plus and clicks its Kind over to Background: the same glass, on any shape, by hand.

steps.reads: Variant, already on Secondary, tooltip none

steps.note: Secondary up close over dense coloured code: inside the capsule the code is a soft pale wash with no readable letters, outside it the code is as sharp as ever, and the button's own dark words read cleanly
The same in dark: the document does not change with the app's appearance, the glass still softens what is under it
A faded rectangle with a Blur added: Kind reads Layer, and the rectangle itself is fuzzy while the code under it stays sharp
One click on Background: the rectangle's edge is crisp again and the code UNDER it is softened, frosted glass
